result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the concept of "othering"—the instinct to divide people into "us" and "them" based on race, nationality, religion, ideology, or any arbitrary distinction. I’d dissolve the mental barriers that make empathy conditional, so that no one’s suffering or joy would ever be dismissed as irrelevant simply because they’re "not like me."

This wouldn’t erase conflict or difference, but it would strip away the illusion that some lives matter less. Wars, oppression, and even everyday cruelty often start with this division. Without it, cooperation would become the default, and solutions to shared problems—climate collapse, poverty, violence—would emerge not from coercion or guilt, but from the simple recognition that we’re all stuck here together.

(And if you’re wondering why I’d pick this over, say, ending hunger or disease: those are symptoms. Othering is the disease.)
